title: Training Loop
description: Standard neural network training loop pattern detailing backward optimization.
name: Training Loop
concept: The training loop is a fundamental pattern in deep learning where a model iteratively processes inputs, computes error, calculates gradients, and updates its weights. At its core, the training loop implements gradient descent optimization: the model processes a batch of data through forward propagation, computes a loss function measuring prediction error, performs backpropagation to calculate parameter gradients, and applies an optimizer update to adjust weights toward lower loss. This cycle repeats across epochs until convergence or a stopping criterion is met. The pattern is framework-agnostic but requires careful management of device placement, gradient state, and training mode toggling to ensure correct optimization dynamics.
applicability: Use the Training Loop pattern when training any parametric machine learning model using gradient descent, including multi-layer perceptrons, convolutional networks, transformers, or recurrent architectures. It is the foundation of supervised learning and applies to classification, regression, generation, and other learning tasks. The pattern is essential when you need to iteratively improve model performance through data-driven optimization. Avoid using a manual training loop when using high-level APIs that abstract training (e.g., model.fit() in Keras, Trainer in Hugging Face) unless you require custom training logic, specialized optimization schedules, or integration with complex data pipelines that standard trainers cannot handle.

when_to_use: Training parametric models with gradient descent
dont_use: Simple training with standard APIs available
Using high-level trainers (Keras fit, HuggingFace Trainer)

decision_flow.question: Require fine-grained optimization control?
decision_flow.if_yes: Manual training loop with custom optimizer

system_interactions.condition: When model contains stochastic layers that behave differently in training vs evaluation mode
system_interactions.effect: Failure to toggle model.train() disables gradient updates to batch statistics and dropout, causing degraded performance and incorrect learning dynamics

system_interactions.condition: When using gradient accumulation to simulate larger batch sizes
system_interactions.effect: Training loop must manage accumulation counter and delay optimizer updates, otherwise gradient semantics break and training diverges

system_interactions.condition: When using FP16 or BF16 for memory efficiency
system_interactions.effect: Loss scaling must be applied before backward pass and gradients unscaled before optimizer update, otherwise numerical underflow occurs and gradients vanish

system_interactions.condition: When using schedulers that depend on step count or epoch
system_interactions.effect: Scheduler must advance at optimizer update boundary, not every micro-batch, otherwise warmup and decay schedules misalign with actual optimization steps

anti_patterns.wrong: Forgetting to zero gradients between steps
anti_patterns.impact: Gradients accumulate across batches instead of being reset, causing gradient explosion and training divergence
anti_patterns.fix: Call optimizer.zero_grad() or model.zero_grad() at the start of each iteration before backward pass

anti_patterns.wrong: Leaving model in evaluation mode during training
anti_patterns.impact: BatchNorm uses running statistics instead of batch statistics, dropout is disabled, and model trains with incorrect behavior
anti_patterns.fix: Call model.train() before training loop and model.eval() only during validation or inference

anti_patterns.wrong: Performing gradient updates without loss scaling in mixed precision
anti_patterns.impact: Gradients underflow to zero in FP16, preventing any meaningful parameter updates
anti_patterns.fix: Use loss scaler (GradScaler) to scale loss before backward pass and unscale gradients before optimizer update

anti_patterns.wrong: Updating scheduler on every micro-batch with gradient accumulation
anti_patterns.impact: Scheduler advances too frequently relative to actual optimizer updates, breaking warmup and decay schedules
anti_patterns.fix: Advance scheduler only at the optimizer update boundary, not every micro-batch

anti_patterns.wrong: Not checking model and data device alignment
anti_patterns.impact: Runtime errors when model and data are on different devices (CPU vs GPU), or silent performance degradation from unnecessary transfers
anti_patterns.fix: Ensure model, data, and optimizer are on the same device using .to(device) and verify with device checks

implementation_notes: The training loop implementation requires careful state management across three phases per iteration: forward pass, backward pass, and optimizer update. Before the loop begins, ensure the model is in training mode (model.train()), the optimizer is initialized with model parameters, and all components (model, data, optimizer) are on the same device. Each iteration should: (1) zero gradients to prevent accumulation, (2) move batch data to the correct device, (3) compute forward pass to get predictions, (4) compute loss against targets, (5) perform backward pass to calculate gradients, (6) optionally clip gradients for stability, (7) apply optimizer update, and (8) optionally advance learning rate scheduler. For validation, switch to evaluation mode (model.eval()), disable gradient computation (torch.no_grad()), and use separate metrics without backpropagation. When using gradient accumulation, maintain a counter and only perform optimizer updates when the counter reaches the accumulation steps. In mixed precision training, wrap the backward pass in a loss scaler context and unscale gradients before clipping. Always include exception handling for data loading errors and implement checkpointing to save training state periodically.
examples:
initialize model_parameters
initialize optimizer_state
initialize scheduler_state
set device = gpu if available else cpu
move model to device

model.train()

for each training_epoch:
    for each batch in dataloader:
        # 1. Move data to device
        features = move_to_device(batch.features, device)
        targets = move_to_device(batch.targets, device)
        
        # 2. Zero gradients
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        # 3. Forward pass
        predictions = model(features)
        loss = compute_loss(predictions, targets)
        
        # 4. Backward pass
        loss.backward()
        
        # 5. Optional gradient clipping
        if use_gradient_clipping:
            clip_gradients(model.parameters, max_norm)
        
        # 6. Optimizer update
        optimizer.step()
        
        # 7. Scheduler update
        scheduler.step()

    # Validation phase
    model.eval()
    disable_gradient_computation:
        for each batch in validation_dataloader:
            features = move_to_device(batch.features, device)
            targets = move_to_device(batch.targets, device)
            predictions = model(features)
            validation_loss = compute_loss(predictions, targets)
            track_validation_metrics(validation_loss)
    
    model.train()

initialize model_state
initialize optimizer_state
initialize scheduler_state
initialize gradient_scaler
set accumulation_steps = K
set micro_batch_counter = 0

model.train()

for each training_epoch:
    for each micro_batch in dataloader:
        features = move_to_device(micro_batch.features, device)
        targets = move_to_device(micro_batch.targets, device)
        
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        with mixed_precision_context:
            predictions = model(features)
            loss = compute_loss(predictions, targets)
            normalized_loss = loss / accumulation_steps
        
        gradient_scaler.scale(normalized_loss).backward()
        
        micro_batch_counter = micro_batch_counter + 1
        
        if micro_batch_counter < accumulation_steps:
            continue
        
        gradient_scaler.unscale(optimizer)
        clip_gradients(model.parameters, max_norm)
        gradient_scaler.step(optimizer)
        gradient_scaler.update()
        scheduler.step()
        
        micro_batch_counter = 0

variations.name: Validation loop integration
variations.description: This variation includes periodic validation phases within the training loop to monitor generalization performance and enable early stopping.
variations.use_when: Need to track validation metrics during training, implement early stopping, or select best checkpoint
variations.benefit: Enables model selection based on validation performance and prevents overfitting
variations.tradeoff: Adds computational overhead from forward passes on validation data

variations.name: Gradient accumulation loop
variations.description: This variation accumulates gradients across multiple micro-batches before performing an optimizer update to simulate larger batch sizes.
variations.use_when: GPU memory is limited but larger effective batch size is desired for training stability
variations.benefit: Enables larger effective batch sizes without exceeding memory constraints
variations.tradeoff: Increases training time per epoch and requires careful management of update boundaries
